role: A global pool of int[] scratch arrays that every GenLayer.getInts draws its output from; reset after each biome query.
scope_reason: Used by every GenLayer call during overworld generation; it has no effect on generated values, only on allocation.

members.name: intCacheSize, freeSmallArrays, inUseSmallArrays, freeLargeArrays, inUseLargeArrays
members.note: Pool state; native allocates with malloc/free per call instead.

members.name: getIntCache
members.note: Replaced by malloc in area(), zoom() and voronoi(); every cell read is written first, so pooling is not observable.

members.name: resetIntCache
members.note: Native frees each buffer at the end of the layer call.

members.name: IntCache
members.note: a class of static members only: nothing in oracle/src constructs it (no `new IntCache`), so its implicit constructor never runs

notes: Not a behavior to port: an allocation pool. For the GPU the per-call malloc in layers.c is itself the hazard (heap allocation, sized by the query); a fixed scratch buffer per layer depth would mirror IntCache more closely. The claim that pooling is unobservable is from reading the layers, not from a test.
